t: The Etruscans believed their religion had been revealed to them by seers, chiefly Tages and Vegoia, and consulted the gods through signs, divination by animal entrails, thunder and lightning.
No Etruscan sacred text survives except the Liber Linteus; the Etrusca Disciplina, a corpus of sacred books, is known only through Roman writers such as Cicero and Valerius Maximus.
Roman haruspices and noble families claiming Etruscan descent carried the religion into Roman public life long after the people of Etruria had forgotten the language.
dyk: The Piacenza liver, a bronze model of a sheep’s liver from the 1st or 2nd century CE, is divided into 40 cells that carry the names of gods.
ev: The shrine at Pian d’Civita in Tarquinia, an early sanctuary of the Villanovan period, is in use, and cemeteries show cremation burial in urns with grave goods
In the Orientalizing Period, dated 750/700–600 BCE, Greek gods and heroes such as Aritimi, Menrva, Hercle and Pacha are adopted into the Etruscan system
Etruscan sanctuaries become increasingly monumental, with major temples, expensive offerings and evidence for animal sacrifice
A freedwoman, Kanuta, dedicates a bronze statue at Campo della Fiera in Orvieto, in an inscription dated 525–500 BCE
The Etruscans are defeated in the Roman–Etruscan Wars, and the remaining Etruscan culture begins to be assimilated into the Roman

f.origin: Etruria, in the Villanovan culture; the earliest evidence for religious practices dates to the Villanovan period, including a 9th century BCE shrine at Tarquinia
f.founder: none: the Etruscans believed their religion had been revealed to them by seers, chiefly Tages, a childlike figure born from tilled land, and the female figure Vegoia
f.scriptures: none survive but the Liber Linteus, of about 800 surviving words; the Etrusca Disciplina, a corpus of sacred books, is known only from Roman writers
f.followers: none: as the Etruscan civilisation was assimilated into the Roman Republic from the 4th century BCE its religion was absorbed into Roman culture, and knowledge of its language and religion soon ceased under the Julio-Claudians
